transcript.statement: The safety of the autonomous driving system is paramount. My requirements (SAF-01 to SAF-07) ensure a robust multi-layer safety architecture, timely execution of Minimal Risk Maneuvers (SAF-02), and continuous monitoring of ODD compliance (SAF-03). These are essential for hazard identification and mitigation. I oppose any requirements that compromise safety, such as EFF-07, which prioritizes smoothness over safety during emergencies. Additionally, EFF-03 conflicts with SAF-02 as it suggests a compromise on the timing of MRMs. I propose that we establish emergency protocols (SAF-07) that allow for the relaxation of smoothness constraints only when absolutely necessary, ensuring safety remains the priority.

transcript.statement: Performance efficiency is crucial for the autonomous driving system to ensure timely responses and optimal operation. My requirements (EFF-01 to EFF-07) focus on reducing travel time (EFF-01), maintaining low jerk for comfort (EFF-02), and ensuring quick execution of Minimal Risk Maneuvers (EFF-03) without compromising performance. I oppose SAF-04, which mandates a jerk limit that could hinder performance during critical maneuvers. Additionally, SAF-07's emergency protocols could conflict with EFF-07, which prioritizes smoothness during emergencies, potentially compromising responsiveness. I propose that we allow for a flexible jerk threshold during emergencies to balance safety and performance effectively.

requirements.text: The system shall implement a multi-layer safety architecture including passive, active, and functional safety mechanisms to ensure collision protection and fail-safe operations.
The system shall execute a Minimal Risk Maneuver within 5 seconds upon detecting critical system failures to safely pull over to a low-risk zone.
The system shall continuously monitor Operational Design Domain compliance and issue a human takeover request when boundaries are approached.
The system shall establish a flexible jerk threshold during emergencies with strict monitoring and robust data protection measures.
The system shall satisfy curvature constraints ($kappa$) to prevent rollover during maneuvers at all speeds.
The system shall utilize iterative quadratic programming to handle non-convex obstacle constraints reliably within a response time of 100 milliseconds.
The system shall optimize path planning to achieve a minimum 30% reduction in average travel time compared to baseline scenarios.
The system shall maintain a jerk value below 0.5 m/s³ during normal operation to enhance passenger comfort.
The system shall achieve at least 95% success rate in optimal speed profile generation during path planning.
The system shall minimize energy consumption during operation by optimizing path and speed profiles, achieving at least a 15% reduction compared to baseline energy usage.
The system shall implement end-to-end data encryption for all user data transmitted to protect privacy and ensure data integrity.
The system shall conduct regular security audits at least bi-annually to identify and mitigate potential vulnerabilities.
The system shall ensure compliance with the Apollo Pilot Safety Report and EM Motion Planner specifications at all operational times.
The system shall document all safety and compliance-related decisions and changes for accountability and regulatory purposes.
